title: ACT ON THE ESTABLISHMENT, OPERATION AND FOSTERING OF GOVERNMENT-FUNDED SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY RESEARCH INSTITUTES
title_original: 과학기술분야 정부출연연구기관 등의 설립ㆍ운영 및 육성에 관한 법률
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISION

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to seek the establishment of an effective national innovation system for science and technology and the business rationalization of management and development of Government-funded research institutes specializing in science and technology, by providing for fundamentals regarding the establishment, support, fostering, systematic management, and responsible operation of Government-funded research institutes specializing in science and technology.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 2 (Definitions) The term "Government-funded science and technology research institute" in this Act means an institute established mainly for research into science and technology with Government funding.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 28, 2014]

Article 3 (Restrictions on establishment of research institutes) No Government-funded science and technology research institute (hereinafter referred to as "research institute") shall be established in breach of this Act. <Amended on May 28, 2014>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 4 (Corporate entity) Each research institute and the National Research Council of Science and Technology (hereinafter referred to as the "Research Council"), established pursuant to this Act, shall be a corporation. <Amended on May 28, 2014>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 5 (Financial resources for operation) (1) Research institutes and the Research Council shall be operated with contributions from the Government and revenue from other sources.
  (2) The Government may provide research institutes and the Research Council with contributions to cover expenses incurred in establishing and operating them, within budgetary limits. In such cases, the Government shall endeavor to secure the financial resources necessary for the sustainable and stable operation of research institutes and the Research Council. <Amended on Feb. 3, 2022>
  (3) Where a research institute or the Research Council, in receipt of a request by a local government, establishes and operates a regional organization under the jurisdiction of the local government (referring to a domestic branch, established and operated with the approval of the Research Council under Article 12-3(1) following a resolution by the board of directors pursuant to Article 24(2)8-2, whose place of location is different from that of the headquarters of the relevant research institute; hereinafter the same shall apply), such local government may provide the research institute or the Research Council with contributions to cover necessary expenses, within the budget. <Added on Mar. 11, 2015; Oct. 31, 2023>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 5-2 (Operation of basic projects of research institutes and research council) Matters regarding the advance notice, advance planning, public invitation, selection, conclusion of an agreement, execution, management, evaluation, change, suspension, etc. of a basic project (referring to a research and development project conducted with the budget directly contributed by the Government to achieve the objectives of establishment under the articles of incorporation) of a research institute or the Research Council shall be determined by the research institute or the Research Council, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 22, 2020]

Article 6 (Business year) The business year of a research institute and the Research Council shall be the same as the fiscal year of the Government.

Article 7 (Special cases regarding permission for use of state or public property, lease or transfer thereof) (1) Where necessary for the establishment and operation of research institutes and the Research Council, the State or local governments may grant permission to use State-owned property and commodities, lease or transfer such property and commodities, free of charge, to research institutes and the Research Council under a negotiated contract, notwithstanding the State Property Act and the Commodity Management Act; and may grant permission to use public property and commodities, lease or transfer such property and commodities, free of charge, to research institutes and the Research Council under a negotiated contract, notwithstanding the Public Property and Commodity Management Act.
  (2) Where any State-owned or public property is permitted for use or leased pursuant to paragraph (1), the term of such permission for use or lease may not exceed 20 years, notwithstanding Articles 35 and 46 of the State Property Act and Articles 21 and 31 of the Public Property and Commodity Management Act. In such cases, the term may be renewed for up to another 20 years.
  (3) Where land owned by a local government is permitted for use or leased pursuant to paragraph (1), permanent facilities may be constructed on the land on condition that such land is purchased at the time the term of such permission for use or lease expires, notwithstanding Article 13 of the Public Property and Commodity Management Act. In such cases, notwithstanding the latter part of paragraph (2), the term of permission for use or lease may continue to be renewed until a period of 50 years elapses.
  (4) Where a research institute or the Research Council needs to purchase land owned by a local government under the former part of paragraph (3), the head of the local government may allow it to pay the purchase price in installments over a period of up to 20 years, notwithstanding Article 37 of the Public Property and Commodity Management Act.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 14, 2021]

CHAPTER II RESEARCH INSTITUTES

Article 8 (Incorporation of research institutes) (1) The research institutes incorporated pursuant to this Act shall be as listed in the Appendix.
  (2) A research institute shall be formed on filing for registration of incorporation at the location of its principal office.
  (3) The matters to be registered at the time of incorporation under paragraph (2) shall be as follows:
  1. The objectives (including the fields of research; hereinafter the same shall apply);
  2. The name; 
  3. The principal office;
  4. The name and address of the president of a research institute;
  5. The methods of public announcement.
  (4) Matters necessary for the procedures for preparing the incorporation of a research institute shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 9 (Articles of incorporation) (1) The articles of incorporation of a research institute shall include the following matters:
  1. The objectives;
  2. The name; 
  3. The location of the principal office;
  4. Matters regarding business affairs and the execution thereof;
  5. Matters regarding property and accounting;
  6. Matters regarding executive officers and employees;
  7. Matters regarding the amendment of articles of incorporation;
  8. Matters regarding dissolution;
  9. Matters regarding the method of public announcement.
  (2) When a research institute intends to amend its articles of incorporation, it shall obtain approval thereof from the Research Council. <Amended on May 28, 2014>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 10 (Guarantee of autonomous management) (1) Each research institute shall be guaranteed independence and autonomy in research and management.
  (2) The head of a research institute (hereinafter referred to as "president") shall take measures necessary for the innovation in the management of the research institute.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 10-2 (Notification of operational guidelines) The Minister of Science and ICT shall establish operational guidelines regarding the following matters that apply commonly to research institutes, and shall notify the research institutes and the Research Council thereof. The same shall apply where the operational guidelines are amended.
  1. Matters relating to organizational operations and the management of authorized staffing levels and personnel;
  2. Matters relating to budget preparation and execution and fund management;
  3. Matters relating to accounting and settlement of accounts;
  4. Matters relating to measures for management innovation;
  5. Matters relating to the evaluation of research performance and management activities;
  6. Other matters relating to the operation of research institutions as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on Mar. 31, 2026]

Article 11 (Presidents and their duties) (1) Each research institute shall have one person appointed as its president.
  (2) A president shall represent the respective research institute in the capacity of director and be responsible for its management.
  (3) A president shall present its operational goals to the Research Council for approval thereof by the deadline prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on May 28, 2014>
  (4) If a president is unable to perform his or her duties for inevitable reasons, the person specified by the articles of incorporation of the research institute shall act on his or her behalf. <Amended on May 28, 2014>
  (5) Deleted. <Jun. 9, 2020>
  (6) Deleted. <Jun. 9, 2020>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]
  [Title Amended on Jun. 9, 2020]

Article 12 (Appointment and dismissal of presidents and their term of office) (1) Each president shall be appointed or dismissed by the chairperson of the Research Council, after prior resolution at the board of directors. <Amended on May 28, 2014; Jun. 9, 2020>
  (2) When a president is to be appointed pursuant to paragraph (1), candidates shall be publicly invited or recommended by the committee for the recommendation of presidents of research institutes prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on May 28, 2014>
  (3) A president shall work full-time and his or her term of office shall be three years.
  (4) Deleted. <Jun. 9, 2020>
  (5) The chairperson shall commence the procedures under paragraphs (2) and (7) no later than three months before the expiration of the term of office of the incumbent president, unless there are unavoidable reasons prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added on Jan. 31, 2025>
  (6) Further matters regarding the appointment and dismissal of presidents shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020; Jan. 31, 2025>
  (7) Notwithstanding paragraph (2), where the research outcomes and business management achievements of a research institute during its president's term of office are found to satisfy the standards prescribed by Presidential Decree following an evaluation of the research institute conducted pursuant to Article 28(1), the chairperson may reappoint the relevant president. In such cases, the board of directors shall adopt a resolution thereon with the affirmative vote of at least 2/3 of all the incumbent directors of the Research Council, notwithstanding the proviso to Article 24(2). <Added on May 28, 2014; Jan. 31, 2025>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]
  [Title Amended on Jun. 9, 2020]

Article 12-2 (Restrictions on application by or recommendation of incumbent directors for president) No director (including the chairperson) of the Research Council as at the date the board of directors of the Research Council resolves on the plan for appointment of the president of a research institute pursuant to Article 12(2), shall be eligible to participate in public campaigning for the president of the relevant research institute or be recommended as a candidate for president.
  [This Article Added on May 28, 2014]

Article 12-3 (Approval of plans to establish and operate regional organization) (1) Where a research institute intends to establish and operate a regional organization, it shall submit a plan for the establishment and operation of the regional organization in advance to the Research Council and obtain approval for such plan.
  (2) The Research Council shall conduct a feasibility study on the plan for the establishment and operation of the regional organization submitted pursuant to paragraph (1); provided, a feasibility study on the plan for the establishment and operation of the regional organization may not be conducted in cases prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as when an urgent establishment of the regional organization is required.
  (3) The standards for the feasibility study under the main clause of paragraph (2), including balanced national development, and policy and financial feasibility, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (4) The Research Council may conduct the feasibility study under the main clause of paragraph (2) by entrusting it to an institution or organization prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (5) Other matters necessary for the procedures for, methods, etc. of the feasibility study shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on Oct. 31, 2023]

Article 13 (Approval of budgets and business plans) (1) The head of each central administrative agency may annually present to the Minister of Science and ICT a written opinion on the order of priority of tasks deemed appropriate for each research institute’s research and the budget required for such tasks, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (2) The Minister of Science and ICT shall comprehensively review the written opinion presented pursuant to paragraph (1) and notify the Research Council of the guidelines for matters that apply where a research institute requests a budget for the following business year (hereafter in this Article referred to as "guidelines for requesting budgets") by not later than March 31 each year, and the Research Council shall notify each affiliated research institute thereof. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; May 28, 2014; Dec. 30, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (3) A research institute shall formulate a budget request and a business plan for the following business year in accordance with the guidelines for requesting budgets by the deadline prescribed by Presidential Decree, and shall submit them to the Research Council. <Amended on May 28, 2014>
  (4) The Research Council shall examine the budget requests and business plans submitted pursuant to paragraph (3). In such cases, it may adjust the budget requests and business plans for the following business year submitted by research institutes, if deemed necessary to coordinate and rearrange similar or overlapping functions of research institutes (including the incorporation, merger, and dissolution of research institutes). <Amended on May 28, 2014>
  (5) The Research Council shall compile the budget requests and business plans of research institutes it has reviewed pursuant to paragraph (4), and submit them to the Minister of Science and ICT by the deadline prescribed by Presidential Decree, and the Minister of Science and ICT shall notify the head of a central administrative agency thereof. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; May 28, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (6) When the State budget is established, each research institute shall submit its budget and business plan for the pertinent business year to the Research Council for approval thereof, as stipulated by the Research Council’s articles of incorporation. In such cases, such research institute may consult with the relevant local government about the budget and business plan for the pertinent business year of its branch, to which such local government has made contributions pursuant to Article 5(3), prior to submitting them to the Research Council. <Amended on May 28, 2014; Mar. 11, 2015>
  (7) When a research institute intends to revise any essential detail of the budget or business plan approved pursuant to paragraph (6), it shall submit the revised budget or business plan, specifying the details of and reasons for the revision, to the Research Council for approval thereof. In such cases, the research institute may consult with the relevant local government about the budget and business plan for the pertinent business year of its branch, to which such local government has made contributions pursuant to Article 5(3), prior to submitting them to the Research Council. <Amended on May 28, 2014; Mar. 11, 2015>
  (8) The Research Council shall submit the budgets and business plans approved pursuant to paragraph (6) to the Minister of Science and ICT, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. The same shall apply where the Research Council approves the revision under paragraph (7). <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 14 (Accounting principles) Accounting of a research institute shall expressly indicate its business performance and increases, decreases, and changes in its property values in accordance with the accounting principles prescribed by the Government.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 15 (Submission of settlement of accounts) (1) After the close of each business year, every research institute shall submit a statement of settlement of accounts for the preceding business year to the Research Council for approval thereof, as stipulated by the Research Council’s articles of incorporation. <Amended on May 28, 2014>
  (2) The statement of settlement of accounts submitted under paragraph (1) shall be accompanied by the following documents:
  1. Financial statements and supplementary schedules;
  2. Other documents necessary to clarify the details of the settlement of accounts.
  (3) The Research Council shall compile the statements of settlement of accounts submitted by research institutes, which have been approved under paragraph (1), and shall submit them to the Minister of Science and ICT by the deadline prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such cases, among the statements of settlement of accounts approved by the Research Council in accordance with paragraph (1), a research institute may submit the statement of settlement of account of its branch, to which a relevant local government made contributions under Article 5(3), to the head of the local government by the deadline prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; May 28, 2014; Mar. 11, 2015; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (4) The Minister of Science and ICT shall submit the statements of settlement of accounts for each fiscal year of the research institutes under his or her jurisdiction to the National Assembly, by not later than 120 days before the beginning of the following fiscal year. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 16 (Internal audits and external audits) (1) The Research Council shall conduct internal audits under the Act on Public Sector Audits for its research institutes and shall have an organization exclusively in charge of conducting such audits. <Added on Jun. 9, 2020>
  (2) The chairperson may delegate part of the internal audit referred to in paragraph (1) to a president. <Added on Jun. 9, 2020>
  (3) A president to whom part of the internal audit is delegated pursuant to paragraph (2) shall establish an organization exclusively in charge of conducting such audit and shall report an implementation plan and the results thereof to the chairperson on a regular basis. <Added on Jun. 9, 2020>
  (4) Each research institute shall undergo an accounting audit conducted each business year by a certified public accountant (including an accounting corporation; hereinafter the same shall apply) designated by the Research Council and shall disclose the results thereof to the public. <Amended on May 28, 2014; Jun. 9, 2020>
  (5) The Government shall endeavor to establish an audit system that reflects the nature of research institutes, such as reducing the burden of external audit for research institutes. <Added on Jun. 9, 2020>
  (6) Matters necessary for conducting internal audits, including the composition and operation of an exclusive organization of the Research Council under paragraph (1), shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added on Jun. 9, 2020>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]
  [Title Amended on Jun. 9, 2020]

Article 17 (Dissolution of research institutes) (1) A research institute shall be dissolved in any of the following cases:
  1. Where the Research Council deems, following its evaluation of achievements in research and business management of a research institute, that it is impossible for the relevant research institute to accomplish its purposes;
  2. Where the Research Council acknowledges that the business for which the research institute is incorporated is advisable to be carried out directly by a State agency, or by any corporation, organization, or individual other than the research institute;
  3. Where an event specified as a ground for dissolution in the research institute’s articles of incorporation occurs.
  (2) When an event specified in paragraph (1)1 or 2 as a ground for dissolution occurs, the Minister of Science and ICT may order the dissolution of the relevant research institute at the request of the Research Council. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (3) Where the Minister of Science and ICT intends to issue an order to dissolve a research institute under paragraph (2), he or she shall hold a hearing thereon. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (4) Where a research institute is dissolved under paragraph (1) or (2), the Minister of Science and ICT shall report such to the competent Standing Committee of the National Assembly. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; May 28, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (5) Where a research institute is dissolved under paragraph (1) or (2), or where part of its functions is abolished under Article 24(2)4, its residual property shall devolve on the national treasury or may be contributed to another research institute governed by this Act.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

CHAPTER III RESEARCH COUNCIL

Article 18 (Incorporation of the research council) (1) The Minister of Science and ICT shall incorporate the Research Council in order to support, foster, and systematically administrate research institutes. <Amended on May 28, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (2) The Research Council shall come into existence upon registration for incorporation at the seat of its principal place of business.
  (3) The matters to be registered at the time of incorporation under paragraph (2) shall be as follows:
  1. The objectives;
  2. The name; 
  3. The principal office;
  4. The names and addresses of executive officers;
  5. The methods of public announcement.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 19 (Responsibilities of research council) (1) The Research Council shall examine the obstacles that research institutes commonly face in the fields of personnel management, budget, evaluation, project management, etc. and shall provide assistance to research institutes for their mutual cooperation in the process of overcoming such obstacles.
  (2) In coordinating and rearranging the functions of research institutes under Article 21, the Research Council shall endeavor to avoid causing any hindrance to the creation of a stable research environment, fully considering the objectives of incorporation, characteristics of business affairs, etc. of research institutes.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 28, 2014]

Article 20 (Articles of incorporation) (1) The Research Council's articles of incorporation shall include the following:
  1. The objectives;
  2. The name; 
  3. The location of the principal office;
  4. Matters regarding business affairs and the execution thereof;
  5. Matters regarding property and accounting;
  6. Matters regarding executive officers and employees;
  7. Matters concerning the board of directors;
  8. Matters regarding the amendment of the articles of incorporation;
  9. Matters regarding the recommendation of presidents of affiliated research institutes;
  10. Matters regarding dissolution;
  11. Matters regarding the method of public announcement;
  12. Matters regarding the secretariat.
  (2) An amendment to any essential provision specified by Presidential Decree in the articles of incorporation of the Research Council shall be subject to a resolution by its board of directors thereon and authorization by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 21 (Projects) The Research Council shall conduct the following projects in order to attain the purpose prescribed in Article 1: <Amended on May 28, 2014; Jun. 9, 2020; Dec. 28, 2021; Oct. 31, 2023>
  1. Planning for research and the direction-setting for the development of research institutes;
  2. Coordination and rearrangement of functions of research institutes (including the incorporation, merger, and dissolution of research institutes);
  3. Evaluation of achievements in research and business management (including business management of a corporation invested by a research institute; hereinafter the same shall apply) of research institutes;
  4. Assistance for collaborative and convergent research between research institutes or between at least two research institutes and institutions or organizations involved in domestic or international science and technology (hereinafter referred to as "collaborative and convergent research");
  5. Assistance for the improvement of research institutes’ achievements in research and the diffusion of research outcome;
  6. Proposal of policies for national innovation in science and technology and the enhancement of competitiveness;
  7. Internal audits of research institutes;
  8. Other business activities necessary for the accomplishment of the Research Council’s objectives.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 21-2 (Collaborative and convergent research projects) (1) The Research Council shall establish and promote policy measures for collaborative and convergent research projects to facilitate collaborative and convergent research.
  (2) The operation of collaborative and convergent research projects under paragraph (1) shall be financed by the Government’s contributions and other profits.
  [This Article Added on Oct. 31, 2023]

Article 22 (Executive officers and their duties) (1) The Research Council shall have not more than 20 directors, including one chairperson and one auditor. <Amended on May 28, 2014>
  (2) Executive officers other than the chairperson shall hold part-time positions.
  (3) The chairperson shall represent the Research Council and exercise general control over its operations.
  (4) The auditor shall audit the Research Council’s business affairs and accounts.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 23 (Appointment of executive officers and their term of office) (1) The chairperson of the Research Council shall be appointed by the President of the Republic of Korea on the recommendation of the Minister of Science and ICT, from among persons recommended by the committee for the recommendation of the chairperson prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; May 28, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (2) Directors (excluding the chairperson) shall be persons specified by Presidential Decree (hereinafter referred to as "ex officio directors") and persons appointed by the Minister of Science and ICT following a resolution by the board of directors with recommendation from the industrial circles, research institutes, and academic circles. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (3) The auditor shall be appointed by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Apr. 5, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (4) The term of office of the chairperson, directors (excluding ex officio directors), and the auditor shall be three years, respectively.
  (5) Matters necessary for the recommendation of the chairperson and directors (excluding ex officio directors) under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 23-2 (Dismissal of executive officers) The appointing authority may dismiss an executive officer (excluding ex officio directors) in any of the following cases:
  1. Where an executive officer falls under any of subparagraphs 1 through 6 of Article 33 of the State Public Officials Act;
  2. Where an executive officer is found significantly lacking in managerial capabilities as an executive officer of the Research Council, following the evaluation under Article 29(3);
  3. Where an executive officer ceases to be able to perform his or her duties for a long time due to a physical or mental disorder;
  4. Where an executive officer inflicts severe loss to the Research Council in breach of an Act or the Research Council’s articles of incorporation;
  5. Where an executive officer severely offends decency in or out of office or is found significantly lacking in good qualities.
  [This Article Added on Apr. 5, 2013]

Article 24 (Board of directors) (1) There shall be established in the Research Council a board of directors.
  (2) A resolution on any of the following matters requires the attendance of a majority of current directors and affirmative votes of a majority of the directors present at the meeting; provided,, a resolution on a matter specified in subparagraphs 2 and 4 requires affirmative votes by a majority of incumbent directors: <Amended on May 28, 2014; Jun. 9, 2020; Oct. 31, 2023>
  1. Approval of a budget, settlement of accounts, or business plan of the Research Council or of a research institute;
  2. Appointment or dismissal of the president of a research institute;
  3. Approval of a research institute’s business goals;
  4. Adjustment and rearrangement of functions of research institutes (including the incorporation, merger, and dissolution of research institutes);
  5. Evaluation of achievements in research and business management of research institutes;
  6. Measures necessary for collaborative and convergent research;
  7. Proposal of policies for national innovation in science and technology and the enhancement of competitiveness;
  8. Internal audits of research institutes;
  8-2. Approval for the establishment of a regional organization of a research institute;
  9. Other matters stipulated by the articles of incorporation.
  (3) The board of directors shall be comprised of directors, including the chairperson.
  (4) The chairperson shall call meetings of the board of directors and chair the meetings.
  (5) The statutory auditor may attend a meeting of the board of directors and present his views.
  (6) Other matters necessary for the board of directors shall be stipulated by the articles of incorporation.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 25 (Planning and evaluation committee) (1) The Research Council may form a planning and evaluation committee, consisting of experts in relevant fields, to assist the Research Council in coordinating functions of research institutes and evaluating research institutes as well as to provide advice on the direction-setting for long-term development in the fields of research under its jurisdiction. <Amended on May 28, 2014>
  (2) The Research Council may organize a management advisory conference, consisting of the chairperson, directors, and the presidents of research institutes to provide advice on decision-making with regard to major policies. <Amended on May 28, 2014>
  (3) The Research Council may establish a committee for research and development strategies, consisting of employees of research institutes and experts in the relevant fields, to provide advice on research planning and the direction-setting for the promotion of collaborative and convergent research. <Added on Dec. 22, 2020; Oct. 31, 2023>
  (4) Matters necessary for the composition and operation of a planning and evaluation committee, a management advisory conference, a committee for research and development strategies shall be prescribed by the articles of association of the Research Council. <Added on Dec. 22, 2020>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]
  [Title Amended on Dec. 22, 2020]

Article 26 (Secretariat) (1) The Research Council shall have a secretariat to conduct its administrative affairs.
  (2) The organization of the secretariat, the scope of duties and the budget of the secretariat, and other necessary matters shall be stipulated by the articles of incorporation.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 27 (Submission of budget requests) (1) The Research Council shall submit to the Minister of Science and ICT, a budget request for contributions for the following business year, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (2) The Research Council shall report to the Minister of Science and ICT on the following matters, as prescribed by Presidential Decree: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
  1. A business plan and budget for each business year;
  2. A business performance report for each business year and the closing statement of revenue and expenditure for each business year audited by a certified public accountant.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 28 (Evaluation of research institutes) (1) The Research Council shall evaluate research outcomes and business management achievements of each research institute in a fair and objective manner, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on May 28, 2014>
  (2) The Research Council shall submit the results of evaluation under paragraph (1) to the Minister of Science and ICT and the Presidential Advisory Council on Science and Technology, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jul. 25, 2011; Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017; Jan. 16, 2018>
  (3) Where the Research Council intends to evaluate the business management of a corporation invested by a research institute pursuant to subparagraph 3 of Article 21, the board of directors shall pass a resolution on the methods, details and targets of the evaluation, and other necessary matters. <Added on Dec. 28, 2021>
  (4) The Minister of Science and ICT shall submit the evaluation results submitted pursuant to paragraph (2) to the competent Standing Committee of the National Assembly within 30 days from the completion of the evaluation; provided, where the evaluation results under the main clause are subject to a meta-evaluation under Article 11(1) of the Act on the Performance Evaluation and Management of National Research and Development Programs, the Minister shall submit the results within 60 days from the completion of the meta-evaluation. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; May 28, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017; Dec. 28, 2021; Feb. 3, 2022>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

CHAPTER IV SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 29 (Supervisory authority) (1) The Minister of Science and ICT shall serve as the supervisory authority over research institutes and the Research Council. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (2) When the Minister of Science and ICT supervises business activities and budgets of the Research Council and research institutes, he or she shall seek an opinion thereon from the Presidential Advisory Council on Science and Technology under the Presidential Advisory Council on Science and Technology Act. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; May 28, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017; Jan. 16, 2018>
  (3) The Minister of Science and ICT shall evaluate the Research Council's performance with regard to the assistance to and administration of research institutes under Article 19 as well as its business activities specified in any subparagraph of Article 21 and shall submit a report on the results of evaluation to the Presidential Advisory Council on Science and Technology. <Amended on Jul. 25, 2011; Mar. 23, 2013; May 28, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017; Jan. 16, 2018>
  (4) The Minister of Science and ICT shall submit the results of the evaluation under paragraph (3) to the competent Standing Committee of the National Assembly. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; May 28, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 30 (Entrustment of business affairs) (1) A research institute or the Research Council may entrust part of its business affairs to a corporation, organization, or individual.
  (2) Matters necessary for the method and guidelines for the entrustment of business affairs under paragraph (1) and the criteria for the selection of a trustee shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 31 (Duty of confidentiality) A current or former executive officer or employee of a research institute or the Research Council, a certified public accountant who conducts accounting audit under Article 16(4) or 27(2) 2, or a person who carries out a business affair entrusted by a research institute or the Research Council under Article 30 shall not divulge confidential information acquired in the course of performing his or her duties or use such confidential information for any purpose other than performing his or her duties. <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 31-2 (Prohibition of use of same name) (1) No person, other than a research institute under this Act, shall use the name of a research institute incorporated under this Act.
  (2) No person, other than the Research Council under this Act, shall use the name "National Research Council of Science and Technology".
  [This Article Added on May 28, 2014]

Article 32 (Expansion of exchange of human resources) (1) Research institutes and the Research Council shall endeavor to exchange their human resources with each other for such purposes as efficiently promoting collaborative and convergent research and development, and shall formulate proactive support measures for the human resources exchanged. <Amended on May 28, 2014; Dec. 1, 2015>
  (2) The Research Council shall endeavor to exchange their human resources with research institutes, small and medium businesses defined under subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of Framework Act on Small and Medium Enterprises, and middle-standing enterprises defined under subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of Special Act on the Promotion of Growth and the Strengthening of Competitiveness of Middle-Standing Enterprises for such purposes as efficiently promoting collaborative research and development, and shall formulate proactive support measures for the human resources exchanged. <Added on Dec. 1, 2015>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]
  [Title Amended on Dec. 1, 2015]

Article 32-2 (Promotion of technology transfer and commercialization) Research institutes and the Research Council shall endeavor to promote the transfer and commercialization of technologies in their possession in order to disseminate and utilize research outcomes, and shall formulate proactive support measures, including assessment of technology; provision of information; conclusion of agreements with related institutions, organizations, etc.; and establishment of strategies for commercialization.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 1, 2015]

Article 33 (Establishment of graduate universities) (1) Research institutes under this Act and the research institutes specified by Presidential Decree from among Government-funded research institutes incorporated pursuant to any Act other than this Act, may jointly found a graduate university defined in Article 30 of the Higher Education Act (hereinafter referred to as "graduate university") with authorization therefor from the Minister of Education in order to train human resources for research. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
  (2) A graduate university shall be deemed a joint institute affiliated with research institutes under paragraph (1).
  (3) The Minister of Science, ICT and Future Planning may designate other research institutes in addition to the research institutes set forth in paragraph (1) to allow them to participate in providing the curriculum in a graduate university (hereafter in this Article referred to as "participating institutes"). Necessary matters in such cases, including the qualification and scope of participating institutes and the procedure for the designation of participating institutes, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (4) A steering committee comprised of executive officers, etc. of the Research Council and the research institutes under paragraph (1), shall be established in a graduate university as an organization to deliberate and resolve on the appointment of faculty members of the graduate university and other important matters specified by Presidential Decree regarding the operation of the graduate university.
  (5) Matters resolved on by the steering committee shall be deemed resolved on by the Research Council and the board of directors of the research institutes under paragraph (1).
  (6) Matters necessary for the appointment of the head of a graduate university, the organization and operation of a steering committee, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (7) Article 5 shall apply mutatis mutandis to financial resources for the operation and management of a graduate university.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 33-2 (Degree courses of graduate universities) (1) A graduate university shall provide courses for doctoral degrees and master degrees.
  (2) Matters regarding the years required for completing a course of study under paragraph (1), semesters, number of school days, curriculum, the prescribed number of students, qualification for faculty members, etc. shall be determined by the steering committee under Article 33 (4), as prescribed by Presidential Decree, and shall be reported to the Minister of Science and ICT and the Minister of Education. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017; ; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) Except as otherwise provided in this Act, the Higher Education Act shall apply to the conferment of master’s and doctoral degrees under paragraph (1), the qualification for admission, the method of admission, etc. In such cases, the "head of a graduate university" shall be construed as "president" as defined in the Higher Education Act.
  [This Article Added on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 34 (Provisions applicable mutatis mutandis) Except as provided in this Act, the provisions of the Civil Act on incorporated foundations shall apply mutatis mutandis to the research institutes and the Research Council. In such cases, "competent authority" in the Civil Act shall be construed as the "Minister of Science and ICT". <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Jul. 26, 2017>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 35 (Legal fiction as public officials for purposes of applying penalty provisions) Executive officers and employees of research institutes and the Research Council shall be deemed public officials for the purposes of applying any provision of Articles 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act to them. <Amended on Dec. 30, 2014>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 35-2 (Notification of commencement of investigation by investigation agencies) When the Board of Audit and Inspection, prosecution, police, or any other investigation agency commences and completes an examination or investigation related to any of the duties of an executive officer or employee of a research institute or of the Research Council, it shall notify the president of the relevant research institute or the chairperson of the Research Council, of the relevant matters and the outcomes thereof within ten days from the commencement and also from the completion of the examination or investigation.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 30, 2014]

CHAPTER V PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 36 (Penalty provisions) Any person who violates Article 31 shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than two years or by a fine not exceeding 20 million won. <Amended on Dec. 19, 2017>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 7, 2011]

Article 37 (Administrative fines) (1) Any person who violates Article 31-2 shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding three million won.
  (2) Administrative fines referred to in paragraph (1) shall be imposed and collected by the Minister of Science and ICT, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jul. 26, 2017>
  [This Article Added on May 28, 2014]

Article 1 (Enforcement date)

Article 2 (Preparation for incorporation of the research council)
(1) The Minister of Science, ICT and Future Planning shall commission incorporators before this Act enters into force for them to deal with the affairs related to the incorporation of the Research Council.
(2) The incorporation committee shall be comprised of not more than 10 incorporators, and the chairperson of the incorporation committee shall be appointed by the Minister of Science, ICT and Future Planning from among the incorporators.
(3) The incorporation committee shall prepare the articles of incorporation of the Research Council and obtain authorization therefor from the Minister of Science, ICT and Future Planning.
(4) Notwithstanding Article 23, the chairperson of the Research Council in service as at the time the Research Council is incorporated, shall be appointed by the President of the Republic of Korea on the recommendation of the Minister of Science, ICT and Future Planning from among three persons recommended by the incorporation committee comprised of the incorporators.

(7) The incorporators shall be deemed dismissed when the transfer of business affairs is completed under paragraph (6).
Article 3 (Special cases concerning term of office of directors of the research council)
(1) Notwithstanding Article 23(4), the term of office of directors (excluding the chairperson and ex officio directors) of the Research Council in service as at the time the Research Council is incorporated, shall be determined differently by the period of one, two, or three years for each director.
(2) Matters necessary for the determination of term of office under paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by the articles of incorporation of the Research Council.
Article 4 (Transitional measures concerning succession to rights and obligations)

(2) The names of the Korea Research Council of Fundamental Science and Technology and the Korea Research Council for Industrial Science and Technology on their registries and other official books shall be deemed the name of the National Research Council of Science and Technology to be incorporated under the amended provisions of Article 18(1).
Article 5 (Transitional measures concerning executive officers and employees)

Article 2 (Preparation for incorporation of the Korea Institute of Materials Science and the Korea Institute of Fusion Energy)
(1) The chairperson of the National Research Council of Science and Technology shall establish the incorporation committee of the Korea Institute of Materials Science and the incorporation committee of the Korea Institute of Fusion Energy in order to perform administrative affairs concerning the incorporation of the Korea Institute of Materials Science and the Korea Institute of Fusion Energy within 30 days from the date of promulgation of this Act.

(4) When authorization is granted under paragraph (3), the incorporators of the incorporation committee of the Korea Institute of Materials Science and the incorporators of the incorporation committee of the Korea Institute of Fusion Energy shall, without delay, file for registration of incorporation of the Korea Institute of Materials Science and the Korea Institute of Fusion Energy, respectively, in their joint names; and shall transfer business affairs to the president of the Korea Institute of Materials Science and the president of the Korea Institute of Fusion Energy.
(5) Upon completing the transfer of business affairs under paragraph (4), the incorporators of the incorporation committee of the Korea Institute of Materials Science and the incorporators of the incorporation committee of the Korea Institute of Fusion Energy shall be deemed dismissed.
Article 3 (Transitional measures concerning budget at time of incorporation)
(1) The Korea Institute of Materials Science and the Korea Institute of Fusion Energy incorporated under this Act may execute the budget of the previous Korea Institute of Materials Science affiliated with the Korea Institute of Machinery and Materials (hereinafter referred to as the "Institute of Materials Science") and the previous National Fusion Research Institute affiliated with the Korea Basic Science Institute (hereinafter referred to as the "National Fusion Research Institute"), respectively, following the previous practices, until each budget of the Korea Institute of Materials Science and the Korea Institute of Fusion Energy is finalized.
(2) When each budget of the Korea Institute of Materials Science and the Korea Institute of Fusion Energy is approved, the funds expended pursuant to paragraph (1) shall be deemed expended according to the approved budget.
Article 4 (Transitional measures concerning succession to rights and obligations)
(1) The Korea Institute of Materials Science and the Korea Institute of Fusion Energy shall succeed to the property, rights, and obligations of the Institute of Materials Science and the National Fusion Research Institute, respectively, out of the property, rights, and obligations that the Korea Institute of Machinery and Materials and the Korea Basic Science Institute have as at the time this Act enters into force, simultaneously with filing for registration of incorporation of the Korea Institute of Materials Science and the Korea Institute of Fusion Energy.
(2) The value of the property to which the Korea Institute of Materials Science and the Korea Institute of Fusion Energy are to succeed pursuant to paragraph (1) shall be determined by the book value as at the day immediately preceding the date of registration of incorporation.
(3) The names of the Institute of Materials Science and the National Fusion Research Institute indicated in the register and other official books as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed the names of the Korea Institute of Materials Science and the Korea Institute of Fusion Energy, respectively.
(4) Acts committed by or toward the Institute of Materials Science and the National Fusion Research Institute before this Act enters into force shall be deemed acts committed by or toward the Korea Institute of Materials Science and the Korea Institute of Fusion Energy, respectively.
Article 5 (Transitional measures concerning status of employees)
Employees of the previous Institute of Materials Science and the previous National Fusion Research Institute shall be deemed to be appointed as employees of the Korea Institute of Materials Science and the Korea Institute of Fusion Energy, respectively, when the Institutes are incorporated.
